audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid warns 'if he Withers you mid-blink your mobility evaporates', and the whole page treats Wither as the reason Kassadin cannot escape. Wither is a move-speed and attack-speed slow; Riftwalk is a blink of fixed 500 range and a movement slow does not shorten it.
audit.why: This is the decisive interaction and the page has it backwards. Wither costs Kassadin the walking between blinks and nothing else — he still leaves any trade Nasus starts. The mirror audit reaches the same conclusion from Nasus's side, where the Nasus player is told he cannot chase a champion escaping on a 5-second blink.
audit.corrected: Stated in tldr, winCon, spikes[1].text, wants.you[1], wants.foe[1], phases[4].why, whys[3], content.mid and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fury of the Sands is described only by 'lifesteal and bonus size'. Riot's text says it grants bonus HEALTH, bonus ATTACK RANGE, a percent-health magic damage aura, a reduced Siphoning Strike cooldown, and bonus ARMOR AND MAGIC RESIST.
audit.why: Two of those matter directly to Kassadin and neither is on the page. The bonus magic resist means his burst lands measurably worse for the ult's whole duration, so a commit timed into it is wasted; and the aura is magic damage, which Void Stone actually does reduce — the one place in this matchup where his passive is on-type.
audit.corrected: Added to spikes[3].text, whys[6] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Siphoning Strike's range is 255 — barely past melee — and nothing on the page says so, while Kassadin's Null Sphere reaches 650.
audit.why: It turns 'last-hit at max range' from a platitude into a measurement. The gap is 395 units, which is exactly the space in which the entire early lane is either safe or lost.
audit.corrected: Written into phases[0].why, tradeGood, tradeBad, content.early and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: diffRating reads 7/10 and both rating lines say 'Tricky matchup', while full.diff reads FAV and the packet records 68.75% over 16 games for Kassadin. The mirror audit set Nasus's side to 7/10 HARD, which is the same lane graded from the other direction — so a 7/10 on this side makes both pages claim to be the hard one.
audit.why: Two pages cannot both be the underdog. The 7/10 here is the inverse of what it should be.
audit.corrected: diffRating 7/10 to 3/10 and both rating lines reworded to 'Favoured matchup'. Nasus's carry threat left at 7.5/10 — his late-game 1v1 genuinely is that dangerous, which is the part the old rating was really measuring.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0] to [6] are the generic Kassadin boilerplate, and phases[6].why still says 'stacked Riftwalks plus Seraph's makes you the best scaling champion in the lobby' on the one stage the content layer explicitly hands to Nasus.
audit.why: Nasus is the rare opponent who out-scales Kassadin in a straight side-lane duel, and the phase text on that exact row promises the opposite.
audit.corrected: phases[0] through [4] and phases[6] rewritten; the two-item row now says take the map rather than the side lane, matching content.late.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carried no numbers — 'bait it before you commit', 'check it before every step-up'.
audit.why: Wither is 15/14/13/12/11s, Siphoning Strike falls to 3.5s at rank 5 and lower still under his ult, and Fury of the Sands is 120/100/80s. Without the 15 seconds, 'bait it' has no unit of measurement.
audit.corrected: All three written into breakdown.cooldowns, plus tradeGood, phases[1].why, phases[3].why and All-In Windows.

audit.whatIsWrong: Void Stone appears as '15% magic reduction' in spikes[2] and content.late; content.mid claims Nether Blade's mana restore is 'quintupled on champion hits'; phases[2].why carries the 'E only charges when spells fly' line; and content.late refers to 'Force Pulse's ability-fed cooldown'.
audit.why: Void Stone has been 10% since V11.24. Force Pulse stopped being charge-gated in V12.23 and is now a 21/20/19/18/17s cooldown that nearby ability casts shorten by a second each — so the content layer's 'ability-fed cooldown' phrasing is right and phases[2].why's 'only charges when spells fly' is wrong, on the same page. No multiplier for Nether Blade's mana restore appears in Riot's text and I could not source it.
audit.corrected: 15% set to 10%; phases[2].why moved to the cooldown model; the quintupled claim dropped and the mechanic kept.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.late tells the player to 'Q-silence the counterplay' and to hunt at two items, on the one matchup where the two-item side lane belongs to the opponent.
audit.why: Null Sphere has no silence, and the sentence also contradicts content.late two clicks away on the same page.
audit.corrected: Silence replaced with the shield, and the late block now excepts this side lane explicitly.

edits.before: Nasus wants to ignore you and stack Siphoning Strike — and early he can. You have only Null Sphere at level 1 with no escape, your Q is mana-hungry and short-ranged, and you have no Nether Blade sustain yet, so you lose every all-in at levels 2-3. Don't try to deny his stacks by force; you'll just eat a Wither-locked Q trade. Last-hit at max Q range and accept that he stacks. One thing to know going in: his Siphoning Strike is PHYSICAL, so your Void Stone magic reduction and Q shield (which absorbs magic) do nothing against his Q hits — your only real mitigation early is distance and not feeding a kill on top of the stacks.
edits.after: Nasus wants to ignore you and stack Siphoning Strike — and early he can. You have only Null Sphere at level 1 with no escape, your Q is mana-hungry, and you have no Nether Blade sustain yet, so you lose every all-in at levels 2-3. Don't deny his stacks by force; you'll just eat a Wither-locked Q trade. Last-hit at Null Sphere's 650 against a Siphoning Strike that only reaches 255, and accept that he stacks. One thing to know: his Q is PHYSICAL, so Void Stone's 10% and your magic shield do nothing against it — your mitigation early is that 395 units of daylight, and not feeding a kill on top of the stacks.

edits.before: Level 6 flips you from helpless to alive. Riftwalk lets you dodge the jungler Nasus loves to set up behind a Wither, blink out of a stack-trade, or punish if he over-extends to last-hit. Lean on Nether Blade now — empowered autos refund a huge chunk of mana (quintupled on champion hits) so your Q stops being a luxury, and a maxed Null Sphere shield blanks incoming magic poke (though not his physical Q). This is your stall window: rush Catalyst into Rod of Ages, farm under tower even through Wither, and climb back to even. Don't all-in a Nasus with W up — if he Withers you mid-blink your mobility evaporates and his next empowered Q crushes you.
edits.after: Level 6 flips you from helpless to alive. Riftwalk lets you dodge the jungler Nasus loves to set up behind a Wither, leave a stack-trade, or punish him for over-extending to last-hit — and Wither cannot shorten a blink, only the walking between blinks, so the slow no longer traps you in his range. Lean on Nether Blade now; empowered autos refund mana so your Q stops being a luxury, and a maxed Null Sphere shield blanks incoming magic poke, though never his physical Q. This is your stall window: rush Catalyst into Rod of Ages, farm under tower straight through Wither, and climb back to even.

edits.before: This is the honest part: Nasus is a hard scaler too, so the 2+ items window you normally take over belongs to him. A full-build Nasus with 200+ stacks, Wither, E armor-shred, and R's lifesteal and bonus size out-duels you in a straight fight — and because his Q is physical, your 15% magic reduction does nothing to save you. So don't play the 1v1. Use Riftwalk's escalating recast charges to chase down their squishies and skirmish where Wither isn't pointed at you, and let Force Pulse's ability-fed cooldown chain into the fight. Let your team body-block and peel the size-buffed Nasus while you assassinate the backline. Win the map, not the side-lane duel.
edits.after: This is the honest part: Nasus is a hard scaler too, so the 2+ items window you normally take over belongs to him. A full-build Nasus with 200+ stacks, Wither, E armor-shred and Fury of the Sands out-duels you in a straight fight — his Q is physical so Void Stone's 10% saves nothing, and the ult stacks armour AND magic resist on top, so your burst lands lighter for its whole duration. Don't play the 1v1. Use Riftwalk's escalating recasts to hunt their squishies where Wither isn't pointed at you, and remember every cast near you shaves a second off Force Pulse. Win the map, not the side-lane duel.

notes: MIRROR: audits/top/nasus__kassadin.json exists and I reused it rather than re-deriving — the silence fabrication, Null Sphere's channel interrupt and shield, Riftwalk at 5/3.5/2s, and Nasus being unable to chase a blink. My side states the same facts inverted and the difficulty ratings are now proper inverses (they set Nasus's side to 7/10 HARD; this side is now 3/10 FAVOURED, where before both pages claimed to be the underdog at 7/10). STILL BLOCKED, EXACTLY AS THE MIRROR REPORTED FROM THE OTHER SIDE: content win[] reads Skill/Nasus/Skill/Skill/Nasus/Nasus/Nasus and full phases[].side matches it, but the mirror's page gives Kassadin stages 3 through first item, and this page's own prose says level 6 flips the lane and first item stalls it to even. 'Skill' to 'Kassadin' is 5 chars to 8 (+60%) and 'Nasus' to 'Kassadin' is 5 to 8 as well — every correction blows the band. The two directions currently contradict each other at four stages and mirror-fix.js will have to arbitrate, or it needs a hand fix. THE MIRROR ALSO CARRIES ONE STALE MECHANIC I did not copy: its content.late says 'Force Pulse charges off nearby spellcasts'. Since V12.23 nearby casts reduce its cooldown by a second each instead — same practical advice, wrong mechanism, and worth aligning. CHAMPION-WIDE: Void Stone is 10%, not 15% (V11.24); the phases[2].why 'E only charges when spells fly' boilerplate is on all 71 Kassadin matchups; and this page contradicts itself on that point, since content.late already used the correct cooldown wording.
